title: A complete pair is henselian
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then the pair $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ALJ (lemma-complete-henselian, line 2482); its proof uses Algebra Lemma 05GI (radical-completion: I is in the Jacobson radical) and Lemma 0ALI (lemma-locally-nilpotent-henselian) for lifting factorizations modulo I^n; Stacks' definition of henselian pair is 09XE, equivalent to the idempotent-lifting one by Lemma 09XI

proof.text: Since $A$ is $I$-adically complete, $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05GI, part (4), applied to an I-adically complete ring

proof.text: For each $n\ge1$, apply the locally nilpotent factorization lemma to $A/I^n$ and its locally nilpotent ideal $I/I^n$. Any factorization of a monic polynomial modulo $I$ therefore lifts to a monic factorization modulo $I^n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ALI, applied to $(A/I^n,I/I^n)$ in the proof of Lemma Tag 0ALJ

proof.text: The lifts at successive levels are compatible: uniqueness in the locally nilpotent factorization lemma, after reduction modulo $I^n$, forces level $n+1$ to reduce to level $n$. Thus the coefficients define compatible elements of the inverse system $A/I^n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ALJ proof, successive lifts and uniqueness from Lemma Tag 0ALI

proof.text: By $I$-adic completeness, the compatible coefficient systems give monic polynomials $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$ and reductions $g_0,h_0$ modulo $I$. The factorization criterion for henselian pairs now implies that $(A,I)$ is henselian.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ALJ proof, final sentence, together with Lemma Tag 09XI
